title: England Beats France 6-4 in Wild Third-Place Playoff
detail: Bukayo Saka scored a hat-trick — including a stoppage-time penalty in the 87th minute — as England beat France 6-4 at Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens, to claim third place, England's best World Cup finish since 1966. Declan Rice and Ezri Konsa also scored as England built a 4-0 halftime lead before surviving a French fightback led by Kylian Mbappé's second-half brace. Mbappé's two goals took him to 22 career World Cup goals, moving past Lionel Messi for the all-time World Cup scoring record, and gave him 10 goals at this tournament — two clear of Messi in the race for the Golden Boot. It was the highest-scoring World Cup match since Hungary's 10-1 win over El Salvador in 1982, and the most goals ever scored in a third-place playoff.
